questions.question: What does CSS stand for?
questions.explanation: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets. It's a language used to control the look and feel of websites.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of CSS?
options: To create the structure of a webpage
To control the look-and-feel of a website (layouts, fonts, colors, spacing, animations)
To add interactivity to web pages
To store data on the server
questions.explanation: CSS is used to control the look-and-feel of a website, including layouts, font assignments, color schemes, margins and spacing, and even animations.

questions.question: Which of the following can CSS be used to control?
options: Layouts, fonts, colors, margins, spacing, and animations
questions.explanation: CSS can be used to control layouts, font assignments, color schemes, margins and spacing, and even animations. It's a comprehensive styling language.

questions.question: What is the best approach to learning CSS according to the resource?
options: Memorize all CSS properties before starting
Learn CSS vocabulary as you design your own creations, using resources as references
Only learn CSS through video tutorials
Focus only on the most common properties
questions.explanation: The CSS vocabulary is expansive and is best learned as you design your own creations. Think of CSS resources as references that you may consult as you go.

questions.question: What is one of the recommended online resources for learning CSS mentioned in the introduction?
questions.explanation: W3Schools — Learn CSS is one of the recommended online tutorials/references mentioned in the CSS Introduction resource.

questions.question: Which resource is described as 'All CSS properties at a glance'?
questions.explanation: cssreference.io is described as 'All CSS properties at a glance' - it's a comprehensive reference for CSS properties.

questions.question: What is the relationship between HTML and CSS?
options: HTML creates the structure, CSS styles that structure
CSS is only used for JavaScript
questions.explanation: HTML creates the structure and content of a webpage, while CSS styles that structure by controlling how it looks and is presented.

questions.question: According to the CSS Introduction, what should you understand about CSS rules?
options: You don't need to understand the rules, just copy examples
Knowing the rules that govern the CSS vocabulary is important to being able to use the language
Rules are only for advanced users
questions.explanation: Knowing the rules that govern the CSS vocabulary is important to being able to use the language. Understanding CSS rules of thumb is essential.
